title: Sparrow Tech — Dedicated Capacity & VPC/KMS Intake
summary: Initial intake with Sparrow Tech to map out dedicated capacity needs. Main asks: predictable reserved GPUs for a hybrid flow (hosted for dev, dedicated for prod), strong tenant isolation, KMS/HSM key management, VPC peering requirements, and a clear burst/fallback plan. They requested security docs and a pilot pricing note and want a follow-up bench run. Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, GA in Q4 2027.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO Sparrow), Marisol (Platform), Tomás (Security)

-- Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete) --
Initial intake for dedicated capacity, focus on reserved nodes, VPC/KMS, burst guardrails.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining on time um this is Jamie from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex Chen: hi alex here, cto, uh excited to dig in.
[00:09] Marisol Vega: marisol, platform eng, i run the infra for inference stuff.
[00:12] Tomás Rios: tomás security. i'll focus on kms, keys, compliance.
[00:15] Priya Narayanan: priya here, i'll be the se on this - i'll ask a few perf questions.

[01:02] Jamie Ortiz: great, objective for today - understand production workload, how many reserved gpus you think you need, isolation reqs, and what a burst / fallback story looks like for you. also any compliance gating. feel free to interrupt.

[02:30] Alex Chen: quick backstory - we built prod on hosted endpoints for internal teams, but as usage hit and some of our customers demanded data residency and more predictable cost, we're evaluating dedicated reserved capacity or a private deployment. we want to keep hosted for dev and non-prod. but for customer-facing features we need dedicated.
[02:58] Jamie Ortiz: makes sense — hybrid is common. what's your current qps and model mix?
[03:10] Marisol Vega: currently about 120 qps across endpoints peak, but that's across dozens of short requests, lots of embeddings for search, and a few long-chat flows. peak p95 lat target is 200–350ms for short gen routes, embeddings can be higher.
[03:30] Priya Narayanan: is that synchronous gen or streaming?
[03:33] Marisol Vega: mostly synchronous now, but we're adding streaming for response UX.
[03:40] Tomás Rios: we also have regulatory constraints — keys need to be customer-managed, and audit logs retained for 2 years, SOC2 plus in flight encryption.

[05:15] Jamie Ortiz: good, one of the core tradeoffs we'll help with is predictable throughput vs cost. reserved capacity gives you dedicated GPU pools and isolation, plus options for warm pools. does Sparrow need strict single-tenant nodes, or will co-tenancy within a reserved pool be OK with strong tenant fencing?
[05:40] Alex Chen: preference is single-tenant for the production customer-facing lanes; non-customer features can be multi-tenant. basically prod-critical traffic needs isolation so noisy neighbor risk is eliminated.
[06:05] Priya Narayanan: we can do node-level isolation — Redwood Dedicated supports tenant-fenced nodes + warm pools. there's also configuration for pre-warmed hot pools to reduce cold-start latency. for single-tenant we typically recommend reserving X nodes mapped to your throughput — we'll run sizing.
[06:30] Marisol Vega: what does prewarm cost look like? any ongoing nightly idle costs?
[06:38] Jamie Ortiz: prewarm cost is part of the reserved commitment; there's a tradeoff between commit size and effective utilization. we can show modeled unit economics in the pricing band. also burst buffers can be configured — you pay for burst capacity on top of the reserved baseline.

[08:22] Alex Chen: for burst — we expect occasional traffic spikes during demo days, roughly 3–5x baseline for short windows (5–20 min). we can't afford timeouts for customers, so fallback is critical.
[08:40] Priya Narayanan: two typical patterns — warm overflow (additional on-demand nodes in the same region) or graceful degradation to a smaller model variant or cached completions for known prompts. Redwood supports both routing policies and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when capacity is low.
[09:05] Tomás Rios: we need to ensure customer data never leaves our VPC — how does Redwood Dedicated integrate with customer VPC and KMS?
[09:18] Jamie Ortiz: for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private deployment options. our Private (VPC/on-prem) option can run control plane in your VPC and we provide connectors to your KMS/HSM. for hosted Dedicated pools we also support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and do not store plaintext keys.
[09:48] Tomás Rios: is HSM required or is cloud KMS ok? we have a FIPS requirement for some customers.
[09:55] Priya Narayanan: we support cloud KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed providers; FIPS compliance depends on the specific KMS and region. we'll need the exact HSM provider and certs.

[11:30] Marisol Vega: ok can you walk through a sample sizing calc? for 120 qps today, with p95 250ms, what sort of GPU footprint are we looking at?
[11:40] Priya Narayanan: quick back-of-envelope — it depends on model family and batch sizes. if you're on a 16B open model quantized, a single A100-class GPU might handle ~60–80 concurrent short-gen threads depending on token velocity. but embeddings are CPU heavy in some pipelines, and long-chat uses KV cache memory. we'll need your token distribution and sequence lengths.
[12:10] Alex Chen: we can export traces, we have 95th percentile tokens ~120 tokens per request for gen, embeddings median 512 tokens. we'll send traces.
[12:22] Jamie Ortiz: perfect — that'll help Priya craft the recommended reserve sizes. we usually propose a pilot with 2–4 reserved nodes to validate throughput and prewarm behavior, then scale to target baseline.

[14:05] Tomás Rios: logging and audit — you mentioned audit logs retained 2 years. do we get direct access or do you push them to our S3?
[14:15] Jamie Ortiz: we can stream audit logs to your logging endpoint or S3 bucket via secure transfer; they're encrypted at rest and we can set retention. we'll include required schema in the security pack.

[15:50] Marisol Vega: about the fallback to cheaper model variant — how automated is that? can we set routes to prefer latency over quality or vice versa?
[16:00] Priya Narayanan: yes routes have policy configs — you can define latency SLOs per route, and the smart router will prefer cheaper variants within quality thresholds, or fall back to a cached response. policies can be per-tenant or per-route.

[18:40] Alex Chen: what's the ownership model for OS updates and infra patches for Dedicated? we don't want unexpected restarts during business hours.
[18:50] Jamie Ortiz: Dedicated includes maintenance windows that we coordinate with you; for Dedicated reserved capacity you get control-plane hooks and we can stagger updates with canary nodes to avoid mass restarts. for Private on-prem installs you get the package and runbooks and Redwood provides update guidance.

[20:12] Tomás Rios: SSO and RBAC — we'll need role separation, least privilege, and SAML with our IdP.
[20:20] Priya Narayanan: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM, and RBAC policies. we can map roles to specific routes, models, and admin actions. we'll include a sample RBAC matrix in the security packet.

[22:01] Marisol Vega: latency requirements — we want p50 < 100ms for some internal microservices, but customer-facing can tolerate p95 250–350ms. can Redwood meet this on Dedicated?
[22:15] Priya Narayanan: for short-gen routes on dedicated prewarmed nodes, yes — hitting p50 <100ms is feasible depending on model and batch settings. we'll need to fine tune batching and sequence length, and consider local KV caches.

[24:30] Alex Chen: how does autoscaling interact with reserved pool billing? we need elasticity but predictable cost.
[24:45] Jamie Ortiz: autoscaling acts on top of your reserved baseline. Reserved provides steady capacity; autoscale can spin up on-demand for burst and you pay for the extra when used. We can model expected spend under your traffic distributions.

[27:10] Marisol Vega: any limits on region choices for Dedicated? we have EU data residency needs.
[27:20] Jamie Ortiz: we can provision Dedicated pools in our EU region; for strict residency we recommend the Private deployment option or Dedicated nodes in a customer-specific region.

[29:00] Tomás Rios: what about preemption? if running on cloud spot instances internally, will Redwood preempt customer workloads?
[29:12] Priya Narayanan: our Dedicated offering uses reserved instances/pools; preemption isn't expected. For cost-optimized pools we can use spot for non-critical workloads but you'll opt-in. Critical prod pools are reserved.

[31:50] Alex Chen: curious — any real-worlds customers in fintech/health that use Dedicated with KMS?
[31:58] Jamie Ortiz: yes, several regulated customers run Dedicated with KMS and audit trails; we can share anonymized references in the security packet.

[33:10] Marisol Vega: about the pilot — what are realistic success criteria?
[33:20] Priya Narayanan: typically: (1) validated throughput target (qps and p95) on your workload, (2) successful VPC peering and KMS integration, (3) fallback behavior validated under synthetic spike load, (4) defined cost model and runbook.

[35:05] Tomás Rios: for the KMS bit, we'll want to run a proof that keys never leave our boundary and that logs are tamper-evident. can we get a runbook for that?
[35:15] Jamie Ortiz: yes we'll provide a KMS integration guide and a test plan for you to verify key usage.

[37:40] Alex Chen: okay timeline wise — we want pilot in 6–8 weeks, then decision for GA by end of Q4.
[37:50] Jamie Ortiz: that's feasible. we'll send pricing bands and a pilot SOW; Priya will propose bench steps.

[40:10] Marisol Vega: small question — caching and embeddings: can you pin certain prompt prefixes or use prefix cache to avoid re-generation?
[40:20] Priya Narayanan: yes we have prefix/KV cache strategies, and you can cache embeddings as well. caching decisions live in the config layer.

[42:00] Tomás Rios: any compliance artifacts we can get right away? SOC2, encryption at rest/in-transit, data residency statements?
[42:10] Jamie Ortiz: we'll attach a security packet with SOC2 report, encryption details, data flow diagrams, and an example SLA.

[44:25] Alex Chen: competitors we evaluated — Anthropic for hosted but pricing drifted; we also considered running fully on prem but that time to market is long.
[44:40] Jamie Ortiz: common tradeoff — control vs speed to ship. Redwood tries to give control while reducing ops burden.

[46:30] Marisol Vega: final question — if we need temporary extra GPUs for a launch day, what's the lead time to prewarm additional capacity?
[46:38] Priya Narayanan: lead time can be minutes to hours if we have capacity in region; for guaranteed prewarming we recommend scheduling and reserving burst capacity ahead of time — that we can model.

[48:55] Alex Chen: good. i'm going to loop in finance and product after this call.
[49:05] Jamie Ortiz: thanks — recap: we'll send pricing + SOW, security packet, bench plan, and schedule pilot kickoff.
[49:20] Marisol Vega: i'll send token distribution and traces.
[49:25] Tomás Rios: i'll send KMS details and compliance matrix.
[49:30] Priya Narayanan: any other questions?
[49:35] Alex Chen: no, thanks everyone.

[50:00] Jamie Ortiz: great meeting, we'll follow up via email with attachments. thanks all.
